title: Mary Wollstonecraft's birth chart
metaDescription: Mary Wollstonecraft's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 6.9° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Moon stands at 13.8° Taurus, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 6.9° Taurus. That falls in the first decan, 0°–10°, sub-ruled by Venus in the classical scheme — a earth sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Mercury holds 27.2° Taurus, Venus holds 2.4° Gemini, Mars holds 22.6° Aries — in the old shorthand, a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste led by wit and proportion; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mars and Jupiter: 0.4° from an exact square. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, Mercury sextile Uranus at 2.1°, and Mars trine Pluto at 2.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Sun stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Three planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Moon in Taurus at 13.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Aries at 22.6° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Capricorn at 22.2° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 earth, 3 fire, 2 water, 1 air; by modality, 4 fixed, 4 mutable, 2 cardinal. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Pluto was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Taurus for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 15.0° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 13.8°.
